claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. I can see you're asking about Alex, who is 11 years old and doesn't live with you.

To assess your eligibility properly, I need to understand your situation a bit better. Let me ask you a few questions:

1. **Regarding Alex being in hospital/residential accommodation for 15 weeks:** You mentioned Alex has been in hospital or residential accommodation for more than 12 weeks. Do you regularly spend money on Alex? This could include things like:
   - Buying clothes, presents, or toys for Alex
   - Providing food or pocket money
   - Contributing financially for their needs

This is an important factor because after 12 weeks in hospital or residential accommodation, you can continue to receive Child Benefit if you regularly spend money on the child.

2. Also, just to confirm - is Alex in a UK hospital/residential accommodation, or is this abroad?

Please let me know about your regular spending on Alex so I can give you an accurate assessment of your eligibility.

## Summary

Based on the information available, I'm unable to make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

**What works in your favor:**
- Alex is 11 years old (under 16), so qualifies as a child
- You contribute £50 per week towards Alex's upkeep, which is more than the Child Benefit rate
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

**The critical issue:**
Alex has been in hospital or residential accommodation for 15 weeks, which exceeds the 12-week threshold. According to Child Benefit rules, you can continue to receive Child Benefit after 12 weeks in hospital or residential accommodation **if you regularly spend money on the child** (such as buying clothes, presents, food, or contributing financially to their needs).

**Unfortunately, I don't have enough information about whether you regularly spend money on Alex** to determine if this exception applies to your situation.

**What you should do:**
I recommend **contacting HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly** to discuss your specific circumstances. They will be able to assess whether your contributions and spending on Alex qualify you to continue receiving Child Benefit despite Alex being in hospital/residential accommodation for more than 12 weeks.

You can contact them by phone or by filling in the online form for child change of circumstances on the HMRC website.
